newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-EX-CHAMPION BAKER-FINCH WITHDRAWS AFTER OPENING 92.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-EX-CHAMPION BAKER-FINCH WITHDRAWS AFTER OPENING 92.

text.p: - Former winner Ian Baker-Finch withdrew from the British Open on Thursday after a nightmare 21-over par opening round of 92.
The 36-year-old Australian, who decided only on Wednesday to play after a long period of inactivity, must have regretted his decision after disaster piled upon disaster at Royal Troon.
Baker-Finch went out in 44 and came back in 48 in a round that included a triple bogey, six double bogeys, five bogeys and not a single birdie.
The 1991 champion at Royal Birkdale, where he wrapped up the title on the front nine on the last day, hated to quit but felt he had no choice.
"The hardest thing is being an Open champion and just wanting to do so well that it puts extra pressure on yourself," the tall, popular Queenslander said.
"I don't want to give in and I feel that in not playing tomorrow I am giving in, but I don't think I should take part."
After a round that one experienced golf journalist called "the saddest thing I have ever seen on a golf course," he said he did not regret his decision to play.
"I played nicely in the practice rounds and I thought I should go and do it," he said.
Baker-Finch has had a torrid time since he won the Open, the demands upon a champion and a recurring back injury combining to wreck his game.
He did not make a halfway cut in 18 U.S. Tour events in 1995 or in 11 last year, and he missed the cut in two European Tour events in Australia at the start of 1997.
"I have not been competing so I'm not sharp," said Baker-Finch, who has been working for four months to prepare for this week.
"When you're playing golf well your mental focus is so much better. When you're birdying and parring you're in a better frame of mind," he said.
"When you're bogeying or worse, you're thinking so much about how many. You start noticing the camera on you, that sort of thing.
"It is very hard to focus on the job when you are shooting horrendously like that. So that's why it gradually got worse.
"Early in the round I wasn't playing that poorly, but then everything went wrong and I couldn't make the putts. Then you're just in freefall and nobody can pull you back," he said.
